overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting two documents used at the September 4 meeting from its minutes, but found the notice topics sufficient, declined to review non-OML claims, and found no intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the 'Staffing Update' notice topic was too vague and should have named the nursing hire and Interim Director of Curriculum.
allegations.key_passage: Second, while we agree that the “Staffing Update” topic listed on the September 4 meeting notice did not include the specific staffing positions mentioned by the Superintendent during the meeting, we find that the topic as listed sufficiently identified the discussions that occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the 'Informational Items' notice topic should have separately listed the Apptegy app agreement.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the “Informational Items” topic was also sufficiently detailed where the Superintendent simply informed the Committee of various projects and activities that had occurred at the schools, including an agreement with Apptegy.com for the creation of a Medfield Schools app.

allegations.summary: Complaint argued the Committee violated G.L. c. 71, § 53 (school nurse hiring) and its own policy on approving the Apptegy agreement.
allegations.key_passage: Because our review concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review and offer no opinion on allegations that the Committee violated other laws or its own policy.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the September 4 minutes omitted two documents used at the meeting: the meeting-guidelines handout and the summer projects document.
allegations.key_passage: Where the September 4 meeting minutes did not contain these two documents in its list of documents used, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the minutes omission was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We also find no evidence that the Committee acted with deliberate ignorance of the law.  Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Revise the September 4 meeting minutes to list the two documents used at the meeting within 30 days of receipt of the letter.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to revise the September 4 meeting minutes within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
